comment: Dr. Richardson is a very nice guy who clearly cares about his students, and takes the time to get to know them. But for his class, there is absolutely zero foresight or organization. He cannot grade to save his life, and when you finally get a grade, its far below what you'd expect. He can't even plan ahead more than a week. Hard to succeed here.

No. I do not recommend this professor. Dr. Richardson is by far one of the worst professors I've had at Richmond. He doesn't provide any practice exams or much practice at all (maybe like 5 questions per exam). The class was unnecessarily hard/confusing. He can be nice and funny, but also sometimes can be sassy.

I could not advise someone more to not take his class. Dr. Richardson reads off his slides and nothing more. You can't reach him outside of class, and honestly, he seems agitated when you don't understand something. He won't read your emails, so don't even bother. Like the class itself shouldn't be hard, but it is very specific.

Dr. Richardson is a nice guy, but his teaching doesn't really go beyond what's on the slides. There are barely any test prep materials, and exams are somewhat difficult. He never answers emails, so it's hard to book times to meet outside of class. Can be dismissive when asked questions. I feel like I'd have been better off taking a different prof.

Dr. Richardson teaches the material on his slides, nothing more, nothing less. If students ask questions in class, he is very dismissive and sometimes even rude, confused as to why we are confused. His exams are fine, but a bit too specific, given how much information we are required to know. I do not recommend Dr. Richardson at all.
Unavailable outside class. Never answers emails. Unclear grading expectations. Insane amount of work. Does not grade anything quickly, so no feedback. Weekly quizzes without enough time for them.

Dr. Richardson is constantly bringing up his aquatic class that no one cares about. Urban biology is so boring. He's a nice guy, but he favors students, which is not right. Has a superiority complex. Overall, fine class so far, just gruelingly boring.

Dr. Richardson was a more lenient grader than the other 202 professors, but he did take a very long time to grade. Other than that, he wants his students to do well. For test questions that most of the class missed, we reviewed them and were able to earn back the points. The only homework was pre- and post-lab assignments—no 202 research paper.

Dr Richardson is great and really makes sure you know your stuff. Class is not easy A but tests and lab grading is fair. Make sure you review lecture slides and do the pre-lab readings. Feedback can lowkey have hints of sass at times, but great/ caring teacher.

This is one of the few classes I'm actually going to miss now that it's done. I mostly looked forward to our Thursday labs on lakes and streams! Dr Richardson definitely cares and makes it fun and brings the class together as a group.
Aquatic is the best class I've taken at UR. Perfect mix of lecture and fun outside labs!

Loved this class! Most of what we covered was interesting and it was much more reasonable work load than most of my Bio classes. Even with COVID we still got out to work with tardigrades and pigeons. Some plant stuff too.

Kinda disorganized, not great at responding to emails, and takes a while to grade. That being said he really cares about his students and is a total sweetheart. Class was pretty easy and didn't require too much studying/work. However, he grades very objectively and material is dry. I enjoyed having him as a prof but wouldn't take again.

Prof. Richardson is super kind and helpful. I had a tough semester, and he was always willing to meet outside of class and spend time working thru class stuff. Hearing from friends, Bio 200 and 202 are just hard classes, but I appreciate how he works with us. Some activities and labs were even kind of fun.

Dr. Richardson is a very nice guy and cares about his students. But he is a VERY subjective grader, does not give clear grading guidelines, and takes WEEKS (around 5-6) to pass back work. Overall, I wish I had taken Brinkerhoff instead.

This is the one class I missed being in person for after corona hit. I didn't love the subject, but Richardson made class fun and our group was good together. After we had to go on line, he did what he could to teach the material without making things even more streesful. He really seemed to care.
